title: when the launcher itself fails (no Python, or Python throws a reserved exit code), the platform shell files a trouble ticket and falls over to Rescue; a command's own failure does not
intention: The platform shell in front of the launcher falls over to Rescue on a launcher failure, writing the trouble file itself when Python cannot run (outline 5.4.3.8.1-3).
why: Measured: 2026-11-20 read of bin/cairn.cmd on akiendell: five lines, it runs bash by a hardcoded path and returns its exit code; it has no fallover, no trouble file and no reserved exit code. bin/cairn on Linux has _floor_refuse (a refusal with one remedy) but files no trouble ticket and does not call Rescue. Outline 5.4.3.8.1-3 says it must. No ticket builds it (open-198248431b60 answered by measurement, 2026-11-19).
traces_to: Law 3 (nothing is known until measured); Law 5 (the repo is the state of the machine: a crossing's record is committed where it lands); Law 9 (green is earned).
how: A hypothesis, not a settled shape (outline 5.4.3.8.1-4, 6.5.3.4-6): bin/cairn.py wraps its own start in a guard that exits LAUNCHER_FAILURE_EXIT (a reserved code, 70) and nothing else uses it. cairn.cmd maps that code, and the absent-venv case it already detects, to a trouble file it writes itself in the trouble store (troubletickets/0, one <slug>.json per defect; a live file at the top is open, so a repeat finds it and increments its counter), then, only at a terminal, execs `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions "read this: <trouble path> <what failed>"` found on PATH. Rescue is Claude Code outside Cairn (6.5.3.4), and `cairn rescueclaude` cannot be the target because the launcher is what failed. Test seams, named: CAIRN_TROUBLE_STORE (store dir) and CAIRN_LAUNCHER_TTY (1/0 overrides the terminal probe, for proofs). Windows only: the Linux floor is the other ticket.

clauses.claim: with no Python reachable (the venv absent), cairn.cmd writes a trouble file in the trouble format into the trouble store and a repeat increments the matching open one rather than writing a second

a launcher failure (the reserved exit code) at a terminal files the trouble and execs the claude found on PATH with --dangerously-skip-permissions and a prompt carrying the trouble file's path (a stub claude on a scratch PATH records its argv)
a verb that exits 1 files no trouble and does not exec claude, and cairn.cmd exits 1
a launcher failure with no terminal (a script, hook or schedule) files or increments the trouble, does not exec claude, and exits loudly non-zero naming the trouble path
a launcher failure at a terminal with claude absent from PATH still files the trouble and exits loudly non-zero naming the trouble path and that claude was not found
bin/cairn.py exits the reserved code when the launcher itself fails before it dispatches, and still exits a verb's own 1 as 1

decisions.text: D1: cairn.cmd files or increments the trouble itself and, at a terminal, execs claude on a launcher failure (clauses 1-5).
D2: bin/cairn.py exits the reserved code only for its own failure (clause 6).
D3: the red-first proof, one tooth per clause.

out: the Linux floor wiring (cast with the Linux ticket's builder, not promised here)

Outline 5.4.3.8.1-3 says it must. No ticket builds it (open-198248431b60 answered by measurement, 2026-11-19).
